# Overview

## Question and hypothesis

**Central question of the project.** Do schizophrenia (SCZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) share cell-type-specific
molecular alterations in the human prefrontal cortex, and could these changes reflect accelerated ageing and affect
neuronal and glial signalling networks?

**Question of this notebook (Q1).** *Which neuronal and glial populations show the strongest alterations in SCZ and BD?*
We answer it at the level of **cell-type composition**: does the proportion of each cell type change with the disease?

**Hypothesis tested.** In the full PsychAD atlas, Lee et al. [1] report that psychiatric disorders are mainly
associated with more neurons, especially deep-layer (L5-6) excitatory neurons. We test whether this signal is found in
the HBCC cohort alone, and whether it is shared by SCZ and BD.

| Notebook | Answers | Gives to the next questions |
|----------|---------|-----------------------------|
| Preprocessing | which donors, which data | donors, Seurat object, pseudobulk matrix |
| **Q1 - this notebook** | ***where?*** which cell types change in proportion | the cell types to study |
| Q2 - pseudobulk DE | *what?* which genes change in SCZ and in BD | the table of all tested genes |
| Q3 - pathway enrichment | *which functions?* | - |
| Q4 - cell communication | *which signals?* | - |
| Q5 - ageing | *accelerated ageing?* | - |

## The principle behind every step

**We compare people, not cells.** A brain that gives 5,000 nuclei is still one person. Treating nuclei as independent
samples (pseudoreplication) makes p-values far too small [2]. The proportions are therefore computed per **donor**, and
the donor is the statistical unit of every test.

## Plan

| Step | What we do | Output |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Composition per donor and per group (description) | Q1-F01, Q1-F02 |
| 2 | Composition test with propeller | Q1-F03 |
| 3 | Sensitivity analyses: does the result hold? | Q1-F04 |
| 4 | Cell types kept for Q2-Q5 | table |

# Setup

| Package | Used for |
|---------|----------|
| `speckle` | `propeller`: cell-type composition test [3] |

| `ggplot2`, `knitr` | figures and tables |

```{r setup}
the.seed <- 2026
set.seed(the.seed)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
})

source("scripts/utils_figures.R")       # common figure style, colours and saving (shared with the other notebooks)
source("scripts/utils_composition.R")   # propeller test (main and sensitivity analyses)
packageVersion("speckle")         # recorded for the report
```

All our choices were **fixed before looking at any result**.

| Parameter | Value | Why |
|-----------|-------|-----|
| `fdr_threshold` | 0.1 | selection rule of Q1, on the Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value [5] |
| covariates | age, sex, genetic ancestry | ancestry is strongly unbalanced between groups; no post-mortem interval in the file |
| `min_ancestry_size` | 10 donors | ancestries with fewer donors are pooled into "Other", so that the model stays stable |
| `nuclei_min` | 20 nuclei | minimum number of nuclei of a cell type in a donor for a usable pseudobulk sample (criterion E7) |
| `donors_min_per_group` | 10 donors | a cell type is retained only if at least 10 donors per group have `nuclei_min` nuclei of it |
| contrasts | SCZ vs controls, BD vs controls, SCZ vs BD | the three comparisons of the project question |

```{r parameters}
# Inputs (outputs of the preprocessing notebook)
proc_dir <- "../01_DATA/processed"            # selected donors, nuclei per donor and subclass
pre_dir  <- "../03_RESULTS/preprocessing"     # E7 table

# Outputs
out_dir <- "../03_RESULTS/Q1_composition"
fig_dir <- "../04_FIGURES/Q1"
for (d in c(out_dir, fig_dir)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Analysis choices
fdr_threshold        <- 0.1
min_ancestry_size    <- 10
nuclei_min           <- 20     # applied in the preprocessing (E7 table)
donors_min_per_group <- 10

# Colours of the groups, the same in every figure of the project (blue = SCZ, red = BD)
col_groups <- c(Control = "grey60", SCZ = "#2166ac", BD = "#b2182b")
```

```{r load}
# Selected donors
donors <- readRDS(file.path(proc_dir, "donor_classification.rds"))
sel    <- donors[donors$group != "Excluded", ]

# Nuclei per donor and per subclass (all nuclei), and E7 table
counts <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(proc_dir, "nuclei_donor_x_subclass.csv"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1))
counts <- counts[sel$donor_id, ]
E7     <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(pre_dir, "E7_donors_per_subclass.csv"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1))

# Covariates of the model
donor_info <- data.frame(donor    = sel$donor_id,
                         group    = factor(sel$group, levels = c("Control", "SCZ", "BD")),
                         age      = as.numeric(sel$age),
                         sex      = factor(sel$sex),
                         ancestry = as.character(sel$genetic_ancestry))
small_ancestries <- names(which(table(donor_info$ancestry) < min_ancestry_size))
donor_info$ancestry[donor_info$ancestry %in% small_ancestries] <- "Other"
donor_info$ancestry <- factor(donor_info$ancestry)

table(donor_info$ancestry, donor_info$group)
cat("Donors:", nrow(counts), "| cell types:", ncol(counts), "| nuclei:", format(sum(counts), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

# Step 1 - Composition per donor and per group

**What we do and why.** Before any test, we look at the proportion of each cell type in each donor. The proportions of
a donor always add up to 100 % (compositional data): if one cell type increases, the others decrease mechanically.

```{r proportions}
proportions <- counts / rowSums(counts)

long <- data.frame(donor    = rep(rownames(proportions), times = ncol(proportions)),
                   subclass = rep(colnames(proportions), each = nrow(proportions)),
                   share    = as.vector(proportions))
long$group <- donor_info$group[match(long$donor, donor_info$donor)]
```

```{r fig-Q1-F01, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
mean_share <- aggregate(share ~ group + subclass, data = long, FUN = mean)

p_Q1_F01 <- ggplot(mean_share, aes(group, share, fill = subclass)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), " %")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean share of the nuclei", fill = "Subclass",
       title = "Mean cell-type composition per group",
       subtitle = "Mean over the donors of each group; all nuclei of each donor") +
  theme_project() +
  theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
p_Q1_F01
save_figure(p_Q1_F01, "Q1_F01_mean_composition", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 6)
```

**Figure Q1-F01 - Mean cell-type composition per group.** Mean proportion of each of the `r ncol(counts)` subclasses
among the nuclei of a donor, averaged over the donors of each group (`r format(sum(counts), big.mark = ",")` nuclei in
total).

```{r fig-Q1-F02, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
p_Q1_F02 <- ggplot(long, aes(group, share, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ subclass, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_groups, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x, 1), " %")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of the donor's nuclei",
       title = "Proportion of each subclass per donor",
       subtitle = "One box per group; each donor counts once") +
  theme_project() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
p_Q1_F02
save_figure(p_Q1_F02, "Q1_F02_proportions_per_donor", fig_dir, width = 12, height = 10)
```

**Figure Q1-F02 - Proportion of each subclass per donor.** Box plots (median, interquartile range, outliers) of the share
of each subclass among the nuclei of a donor, per group. Y axes are free: compare the groups within a panel, not between
panels.

::: {.callout-tip title="How to read"}
In each panel, a box shifted up or down compared with the controls suggests a change in proportion. Overlapping boxes
mean that the variability between donors is larger than the difference between groups.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Interpretation"}
- **The variability between donors is huge** (oligodendrocytes from almost 0 % to
  `r round(100 * max(proportions[, "Oligo"]))` % of a donor's nuclei, astrocytes up to
  `r round(100 * max(proportions[, "Astro"]))` %), and the boxes of the three groups overlap in every panel.
- Two shifts are visible by eye: fewer oligodendrocytes in BD and fewer microglia in SCZ. This is description only; the
  test is Step 2.
- The proportion of oligodendrocytes mostly depends on how much white matter was dissected with the cortex: a difference
  there may be a dissection effect.
- Deep-layer neurons are absent in some donors (for example EN_L6_IT_2 in `r sum(counts[, "EN_L6_IT_2"] == 0)` donors),
  probably a dissection effect too.
:::

# Step 2 - Composition test with propeller

**What we do and why.** Proportions cannot be compared with a simple test, because they always add up to 100 %: if one
cell type increases, the others decrease. `propeller` [3] is a method made for this situation:

1. for each donor, compute the share of each cell type;
2. transform these shares so that they can be analysed like ordinary measurements;
3. for each cell type, compare the groups while taking age, sex and ancestry into account (`limma` [4]);
4. correct for the fact that `r ncol(counts)` cell types are tested (false discovery rate, FDR [5]).

```{r propeller}
three_comparisons <- list(c("Control", "SCZ"), c("Control", "BD"), c("BD", "SCZ"))   # c(reference, tested)
main <- test_composition(counts, donor_info, three_comparisons)

# One row per subclass, one column per contrast
short_name <- c(SCZ_vs_Control = "SCZ_vs_Ctl", BD_vs_Control = "BD_vs_Ctl", SCZ_vs_BD = "SCZ_vs_BD")
results <- data.frame(subclass = unique(main$subclass))
for (k in c("FDR", "ratio", "t")) for (contrast in names(short_name)) {
  part <- main[main$contrast == contrast, ]
  results[[paste0(k, "_", short_name[[contrast]])]] <- part[[k]][match(results$subclass, part$subclass)]
}
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Reading the propeller output"}
In the source code of `propeller.ttest`, `Tstatistic`, `P.Value` and `FDR` come from the **adjusted** model (age, sex,
ancestry), whereas `PropRatio` is **not adjusted**: it is the ratio of the raw mean proportions of the two groups. We
therefore read the direction of the adjusted effect on the t statistic.
:::

```{r fig-Q1-F03, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
contrast_labels <- c(SCZ_vs_Control = "SCZ vs controls", BD_vs_Control = "BD vs controls", SCZ_vs_BD = "SCZ vs BD")
effects <- main
effects$contrast    <- factor(contrast_labels[effects$contrast], levels = contrast_labels)
effects$significant <- effects$FDR < fdr_threshold

p_Q1_F03 <- ggplot(effects, aes(t, reorder(subclass, t), shape = significant)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 16), name = paste0("FDR < ", fdr_threshold)) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted t statistic (negative = fewer nuclei of this type in the first group)", y = NULL,
       title = "Change in proportion of each subclass",
       subtitle = paste0("propeller (logit), adjusted for age, sex and genetic ancestry; ", nrow(counts), " donors")) +
  theme_project()
p_Q1_F03
save_figure(p_Q1_F03, "Q1_F03_propeller_t", fig_dir, width = 11, height = 7)

significant <- effects[effects$significant, c("contrast", "subclass", "t", "FDR")]
significant$t   <- round(significant$t, 2)
significant$FDR <- signif(significant$FDR, 2)
rownames(significant) <- NULL
significant
```

**Figure Q1-F03 - Change in proportion of each cell subclass in SCZ and BD.** Adjusted t statistic of the propeller test
(logit transformation, linear model with age, sex and genetic ancestry) for each of the `r ncol(counts)` subclasses, in
SCZ vs controls, BD vs controls and SCZ vs BD (`r nrow(counts)` donors). Filled dots: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR <
`r fdr_threshold`. The table below the figure gives the significant results.

::: {.callout-tip title="How to read"}
Each dot is a subclass. Left of the vertical line: fewer nuclei of this type in the first group of the comparison (for
example fewer in SCZ than in controls). The further from 0, the stronger the evidence. Only filled dots pass the threshold
fixed in advance.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Interpretation"}
- **Microglia are less abundant in SCZ (FDR `r signif(results$FDR_SCZ_vs_Ctl[results$subclass == "Micro"], 2)`) and in
  BD (FDR `r signif(results$FDR_BD_vs_Ctl[results$subclass == "Micro"], 2)`) than in controls**, with no difference
  between the two disorders (FDR `r signif(results$FDR_SCZ_vs_BD[results$subclass == "Micro"], 2)` for SCZ vs BD): a
  shared change of the immune compartment. Perivascular macrophages (PVM) show the same trend without passing the
  threshold. This is an association, not a mechanism: treatment or the conditions of death are possible explanations
  that this cohort cannot test.
- **Oligodendrocytes are less abundant in BD** (FDR `r signif(results$FDR_BD_vs_Ctl[results$subclass == "Oligo"], 2)`),
  but this is the result most exposed to a dissection effect.
- **SCZ vs BD: no significant difference.** With limited power and ancestry confounding, this means "no difference
  detected", not "no difference".
- **Deep-layer (L5-6) neurons: no change.** The increase reported in the full atlas [1] is not found in HBCC alone, which
  has far fewer donors.
:::

# Step 3 - Does the result hold? (sensitivity analyses)

**What we do and why.** We run the same test again, changing one thing at a time. These analyses were decided before
seeing the results. A result that holds in every variant is robust; a result that disappears has to be discussed.

```{r sensitivity}
deep_layers    <- c("EN_L5_6_NP", "EN_L6_IT_1", "EN_L6_IT_2", "EN_L6B", "EN_L6_CT")
key_subclasses <- c("Micro", "Oligo", deep_layers)

# B. without the donors with fewer than 1,000 nuclei (imprecise proportions)
keep_B <- rowSums(counts) >= 1000
# C. without the oligodendrocytes: proportions recomputed among the other nuclei
counts_C <- counts[, colnames(counts) != "Oligo"]
# D. SCZ vs controls in donors of African ancestry only
keep_D <- donor_info$ancestry == "African" & donor_info$group %in% c("Control", "SCZ")
# E. BD vs controls in donors of European ancestry only
keep_E <- donor_info$ancestry == "European" & donor_info$group %in% c("Control", "BD")
# F. without the donors with 0 nuclei in a deep layer (dissection effect)
missing_deep_layer <- apply(counts[, deep_layers] == 0, 1, any)
keep_F <- !missing_deep_layer

all_variants <- rbind(
  data.frame(analysis = "A_main",                             main),
  data.frame(analysis = "B_without_donors_under_1000_nuclei", test_composition(counts[keep_B, ], donor_info[keep_B, ], three_comparisons)),
  data.frame(analysis = "C_without_oligodendrocytes",         test_composition(counts_C, donor_info, three_comparisons)),
  data.frame(analysis = "D_African_ancestry_only",            test_composition(counts[keep_D, ], donor_info[keep_D, ], list(c("Control", "SCZ")))),
  data.frame(analysis = "E_European_ancestry_only",           test_composition(counts[keep_E, ], donor_info[keep_E, ], list(c("Control", "BD")))),
  data.frame(analysis = "F_all_deep_layers_present",          test_composition(counts[keep_F, ], donor_info[keep_F, ], three_comparisons)))

sensitivity <- all_variants[all_variants$subclass %in% key_subclasses, c("analysis", "subclass", "contrast", "t", "FDR")]
sensitivity$t   <- round(sensitivity$t, 2)
sensitivity$FDR <- signif(sensitivity$FDR, 2)
rownames(sensitivity) <- NULL

# Are the donors without a deep layer distributed in the same way in the three groups? (donor-level test)
deep_table  <- table(missing_deep_layer, donor_info$group)
deep_fisher <- fisher.test(deep_table)
deep_table
```

| Variant | Donors | Question |
|---------|--------|----------|
| A. main analysis | `r nrow(counts)` | reference |
| B. without donors with fewer than 1,000 nuclei | `r sum(keep_B)` | do imprecise proportions drive the result? |
| C. without oligodendrocytes | `r nrow(counts)` | does the drop of oligodendrocytes create effects elsewhere? |
| D. donors of African ancestry only | `r sum(keep_D & donor_info$group == "Control")` controls, `r sum(keep_D & donor_info$group == "SCZ")` SCZ | does the SCZ effect hold without the ancestry imbalance? |
| E. donors of European ancestry only | `r sum(keep_E & donor_info$group == "Control")` controls, `r sum(keep_E & donor_info$group == "BD")` BD | does the BD effect hold without the ancestry imbalance? |
| F. donors with all deep layers present | `r sum(keep_F)` | does the dissection of deep layers change the result? |

```{r fig-Q1-F04, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
sens <- sensitivity[sensitivity$subclass %in% c("Micro", "Oligo") &
                    sensitivity$contrast %in% c("SCZ_vs_Control", "BD_vs_Control"), ]
sens$panel <- paste0(sens$subclass, ", ", sub("_vs_Control", " vs controls", sens$contrast))
variant_labels <- c(A_main                             = "A. main analysis",
                    B_without_donors_under_1000_nuclei = "B. without donors < 1,000 nuclei",
                    C_without_oligodendrocytes         = "C. without oligodendrocytes",
                    D_African_ancestry_only            = "D. African ancestry only",
                    E_European_ancestry_only           = "E. European ancestry only",
                    F_all_deep_layers_present          = "F. all deep layers present")
sens$variant     <- factor(variant_labels[sens$analysis], levels = rev(variant_labels))
sens$significant <- sens$FDR < fdr_threshold

p_Q1_F04 <- ggplot(sens, aes(t, variant, shape = significant)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 16), name = paste0("FDR < ", fdr_threshold)) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted t statistic", y = "Variant",
       title = "Microglia and oligodendrocytes in every sensitivity analysis",
       subtitle = "Same propeller model; one thing changed at a time") +
  theme_project()
p_Q1_F04
save_figure(p_Q1_F04, "Q1_F04_sensitivity", fig_dir, width = 10, height = 5)

micro_D <- sensitivity[sensitivity$analysis == "D_African_ancestry_only" & sensitivity$subclass == "Micro", ]
bd_E    <- sensitivity[sensitivity$analysis == "E_European_ancestry_only" & sensitivity$subclass %in% c("Micro", "Oligo"), ]
```

**Figure Q1-F04 - Robustness of the main Q1 results.** Adjusted t statistic of the propeller test for microglia and
oligodendrocytes in the main analysis (A) and in five sensitivity analyses (B-F, see the table above). Filled dots: FDR <
`r fdr_threshold`. Missing dots: the comparison was not run in that variant.

::: {.callout-tip title="How to read"}
If the dots of a panel stay on the same side of 0 in every variant, the direction of the effect is robust. A dot moving
towards 0 in a smaller variant can reflect a loss of power rather than a disappearing effect.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Interpretation"}
- **Microglia in SCZ: the most robust result.** Same direction in every variant, and the strongest effect in donors of
  African ancestry only (t = `r micro_D$t`, FDR `r micro_D$FDR`): ancestry does not explain it.
- **Microglia and oligodendrocytes in BD:** same direction everywhere, but weaker in donors of European ancestry only
  (FDR `r paste(bd_E$FDR, collapse = " and ")`). Loss of power (`r sum(keep_E)` donors instead of `r nrow(counts)`) or
  partly an ancestry effect: we cannot tell them apart.
- Removing oligodendrocytes does not create any effect on neurons (variant C): no mechanical artefact of composition.
- Donors without deep layers are not unbalanced between groups
  (`r paste0(round(100 * prop.table(deep_table, 2)["TRUE", ]), " % of ", colnames(deep_table), collapse = ", ")`;
  Fisher exact test p = `r signif(deep_fisher$p.value, 2)`).
:::

# Step 4 - Cell types kept for Q2 to Q5

**What we do and why.** The rule was fixed before the analysis: a subclass is kept if its FDR is below
`r fdr_threshold` in at least one comparison, plus the deep-layer (L5-6) excitatory neurons kept *a priori* from the
hypothesis of [1], provided that the subclass is frequent enough for Q2 (at least `r donors_min_per_group` donors per
group with `r nuclei_min` nuclei or more, E7 table of the preprocessing).

```{r kept}
smallest_FDR <- pmin(results$FDR_SCZ_vs_Ctl, results$FDR_BD_vs_Ctl, results$FDR_SCZ_vs_BD)
results$significant     <- smallest_FDR < fdr_threshold
results$a_priori_L5_6   <- grepl("^EN_L5|^EN_L6", results$subclass)
results$usable_E7       <- apply(E7, 1, min)[results$subclass] >= donors_min_per_group
results$retained_for_Q2 <- (results$significant | results$a_priori_L5_6) & results$usable_E7
results <- results[order(smallest_FDR), ]

retained_subclasses <- results$subclass[results$retained_for_Q2]
data.frame(subclass = retained_subclasses,
           reason   = ifelse(results$significant[results$retained_for_Q2],
                             paste0("significant in Q1 (FDR < ", fdr_threshold, ")"),
                             "kept a priori (hypothesis of Lee et al.), not changed in Q1"))

# Too rare for a pseudobulk analysis
results$subclass[!results$usable_E7]

write.csv(results, file.path(out_dir, "Q1_propeller_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(sensitivity, file.path(out_dir, "Q1_sensitivity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(retained_subclasses, file.path(out_dir, "Q1_retained_subclasses.txt"))   # read by Q2 to Q5
```

::: {.callout-important title="Interpretation"}
- Two subclasses are kept **on result** (microglia, oligodendrocytes) and five **on hypothesis** (L5-6 neurons): the
  L5-6 neurons are not "altered" in Q1.
- `r paste(results$subclass[!results$usable_E7], collapse = ", ")` are too rare for a pseudobulk analysis and are left
  out.
:::

# Synthesis: answer to Q1

| Element | Result | Figure |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Donors analysed | `r nrow(counts)` (`r sum(donor_info$group == "Control")` controls, `r sum(donor_info$group == "SCZ")` SCZ, `r sum(donor_info$group == "BD")` BD), one brain bank | preprocessing |
| Main limit | genetic ancestry confounded with diagnosis | preprocessing |
| Main composition change | fewer microglia in SCZ and in BD, shared | Q1-F03 |
| Most robust result | fewer microglia in SCZ, also in African-ancestry donors only | Q1-F04 |
| Fragile result | fewer oligodendrocytes in BD (dissection, ancestry) | Q1-F03, Q1-F04 |
| SCZ vs BD | no difference detected | Q1-F03 |
| Hypothesis of [1] (more L5-6 neurons) | not found in HBCC | Q1-F03 |

**In one sentence:** in the HBCC cohort, the only robust change in cell-type composition is a lower proportion of
microglia, shared by schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and clearer in schizophrenia, where it persists after
stratification on ancestry.

# Limits

- **Ancestry confounded with diagnosis** (severity 5/5): adjusted for and stratified, but it cannot be removed.
- **Dissection** (4/5): the share of oligodendrocytes depends on the white matter dissected; deep layers are missing in
  some donors.
- **Power** (3/5): `r sum(donor_info$group == "SCZ")` SCZ and `r sum(donor_info$group == "BD")` BD donors; a
  non-significant result is not evidence of no effect.
- **No post-mortem interval and no information on treatments** (3/5): covariates limited to age, sex and ancestry.
- **Donors with few nuclei** (2/5): `r sum(rowSums(counts) < 1000)` donors with fewer than 1,000 nuclei (minimum
  `r min(rowSums(counts))`); variant B.
- **Observational post-mortem study**: we report associations, never causes.
